weaknesses: The central efficiency claims are insufficiently evaluated. The paper reports parameter counts but no peak VRAM, activation memory, throughput, FLOPs, or wall-clock measurements, so the abstract's claim of comparable training time is unsupported. Critical matched controls are missing, including the original iterated Q-Network, an equal-compute shared multi-head model whose heads regress the same target, and an online ensemble-shared-features baseline. Since iS-QN samples behavior from multiple heads and applies K auxiliary TD losses to the shared torso, the gains cannot be confidently attributed to consecutive Bellman iterations rather than exploration, ensembling, or multi-task representation learning.

The Bellman-iteration interpretation is only heuristic: although the first linear head is frozen, its represented Q-function changes whenever the shared feature extractor changes, and all heads are coupled through that extractor. Hyperparameter fairness is questionable. The evidence is limited to selected 15- or 10-game Atari subsets, one offline dataset fraction, and discrete actions. The main claims therefore do not yet demonstrate robustness over a full benchmark, other domains, continuous control, or genuinely large models.
